paragraphs: Friend, this is the heavy one. Moses lays out what happens if Israel walks away from the LORD, and he doesn't soften it. I think it's meant to be hard to hear, because it shows how seriously God takes the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:15). The blessings and the curses are two sides of one choice: obey the LORD, or forsake Him.

Now look at the reason Moses gives. It isn't that they forgot a rule. It's "Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart in all your abundance" (Deuteronomy 28:47). They had plenty, and the problem was a heart that stopped serving Him gladly. So the lesson for you is that God cares about the heart behind the doing, not just the doing.

Here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today. Moses says it all comes from not being careful to observe His words and to fear "this glorious and awesome name" (Deuteronomy 28:58). That means the best thing a baker can do is stay close to the LORD and keep His Word in the middle of the kitchen. The story isn't over, because Moses still has more to say to the people.
